# AI features

Applies when the change touches: a model call, retrieval, embeddings, or fine-tuning. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Classify the feature by EU AI Act tier and NIST AI RMF risk: a prohibited use stops, a high-risk use is major with the compliance analyst. |
| Specify | A golden dataset and eval thresholds in the Acceptance; a regression eval for every behavior the change must keep. |
| Specify | Model, prompt, and parameter versions pinned in the Spec; the model card update planned as a documentation Task. |
| Implement | Model output is untrusted input: validate structured outputs, bound cost and latency, guard against prompt injection (LLM01) and data leakage (LLM02). |
| Review | The evals ran on head against the thresholds; failure modes and human oversight are documented. |
| Ship | Canary with eval-based and cost-based rollback triggers; prompts and outputs logged under the privacy rules. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Eval suite (emerging) | the golden-dataset thresholds hold on head | promptfoo, Inspect, or the repo's own eval runner |
| Regression evals | kept behavior did not move | the same runner on the previous golden set |
| Injection probes (emerging) | prompt injection and jailbreak probes are blocked | garak or a promptfoo red-team run |
| Cost and latency budget | each request stays within the budget | the eval runner's cost and latency metrics with thresholds |
| PII scan (model outputs) | no personal data in logs or outputs | Presidio or an equivalent scanner over the eval outputs |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
